Multicast group size hides a trade-off in multi-cell NOMA: larger groups suffer unstable information freshness but lower inter-cell interference, while smaller groups draw more interference yet lose less freshness when a transmission fails. This work proposes an AoI-aware interference mitigation (AIM) scheme that dynamically adjusts group size, scheduling, and power allocation; under the paper's AoI model and a cap on the number of groups scheduled per slot, its scheduling strategy is shown to minimize the total AoI, and a bandit-based grouping approach outperforms random, fixed, and genetic-algorithm groupings. To our knowledge, this is the first study of AoI for task-oriented IoT applications in multi-cell multicast NOMA networks.
